Alexander Singer
Alexander Singer( born 18 April 1928, in New York City, New York) is an American director. He began his career behind the camera in 1951 as a cinematographer on the short documentary" Day of the Fight", directed by his high school friend, Stanley Kubrick. Singer himself turned to directing a decade later with the film," A Cold Wind in August". Although he would direct other feature films, such as the Lee Van Cleef western," Captain Apache"( 1971), and" Glass Houses"( 1972), a film of the book which his wife, Judith Singer, wrote, the bulk of Singer's credits are in television. The long list of series to which Singer has lent his directorial talents include" Dr. Kildare The F.B.I.Alias Smith and JonesNakiaPolice WomanCagney& LaceyMacGyver", six episodes of" The Monkees", and three" Star Trek" series:,, and.
